answer: Sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to complete a unique, time-bound computational puzzle tied to its public key before it may transact. A verifier issues a fresh challenge, the raven test, and only accepts work that cannot be replayed across identities. Like a jade seal that is cheap to check but costly to forge, the puzzle makes each fake identity pay full price, so an attacker building a hollow army of clones faces a cost that grows linearly with every clone instead of getting them free.
